TODDLER ROOM LESSON · TODDLER ROOM · AGES 1–3 YEARS

Pillow — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches "pillow" through the flop: wobble like a sleepy robot, land on the pillow, sigh like the day is over — because it is.

What is this?

The pillow is the soft square at the head of the bed where the tired head lands — the last stop of every bedtime.

What does it mean?

The flop-sigh is secret training: the exaggerated sigh slows the breathing, and slow breathing is the body’s own sleep switch. Comedy first, physiology second.

What does the child need to know?

You need the pillow (on the bed, not the floor), a teddy for rehearsal and the three-beat game: wobble… flop… "aaaaah." The sigh is the star; coach it proudly.

Why this matters

Toddlers cannot be ordered to relax, but they can be invited to perform a sigh. The game rehearses the exact exhale that falling asleep needs — nightly, joyfully, free.

What it teaches

Body regulation, head-neck control in the flop, routine vocabulary, and the muscle memory of exhale-and-settle.

Words to learn

pillowheadflopsighsoftmmm

Say this to your child

“"Pillow! The soft, squishy pillow. Wobble like a sleepy robot… flop! Your head lands… aaaaah. Mmm. The pillow holds your head all night. Goodnight, head!"”

Step by step

  1. Daytime rehearsal: teddy flops first — "wobble, wobble… FLOP! aaaaah." The toddler attends to the comedy.
  2. Offer the turn: the toddler’s flop onto the pillow. Coach the sigh: "bigger… aaaaah!"
  3. Name the landing: "your head on the pillow — mmm, soft."
  4. At bedtime, the same three beats, slower: wobble (a sleepy sway), flop (head down), sigh (long and soft).
  5. Fade the comedy, keep the sigh: within a week the flop IS the goodnight.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "pillow" sits under a plump blue pillow — the square, soft landing every bedtime promises.

Ask your child

"Where does your head go?" (on the pillow) "Show me the flop!" "What does the sigh sound like?" (aaaaah)

What your child can say or do

Your child might flop and sigh on request, demand "flop again!", or land mid-yawn at bedtime — the tool, self-deploying.

Out in the real world

Pillows are universal: the sofa cushion, grandma’s guest pillow, the pool lounger. Any soft landing is "a pillow moment" — sigh included.

Try it together

Pillow Mountain: every cushion in the house, one summit, flops all round. The expedition ends flat, sighing, gloriously done.

Understanding check

Ask: "What is this?" (pillow) "Where does the head land?" "Show me the sigh!" — name, flop, exhale: sleep is approaching.

This lesson pairs with the Pillow flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Toddler Room.
